ICB-01.estimand: Technical-failure and low-complexity risks over all attempts, plus conditional score change among jointly scoring-valid and historical-filter pairs.
ICB-01.control: Matched-norm random direction and the all-layer steering arm where both arms remain evaluable.
ICB-01.limitation: Low-complexity outputs can remain scoring-valid. The claim concerns the historical filter and does not call every low-complexity sequence invalid.

ICB-02.estimand: Validation performance of the fixed sequence-composition scores for peptide MHC-II binding and observed T-cell response in the saved deduplicated cohorts.
ICB-02.statistical_unit: Peptide or labeled sequence, according to the source cohort.
ICB-02.control: Evaluation against the biological endpoint rather than only the binding surrogate.
ICB-02.limitation: The available work evaluates the listed scores in fixed cohorts. It does not prove that sequence cannot predict T-cell response, and it does not run a steering intervention.

ICB-03.estimand: Paired random-fold minus organism-grouped validation performance for fixed length-only, composition-only, and composition-plus-length models.
ICB-03.statistical_unit: Sequence, with organism-level weighting and organism-clustered uncertainty.
ICB-03.control: Identical random and organism-grouped folds for prespecified length-only, composition-only, and composition-plus-length models.
ICB-03.limitation: A performance drop under grouped validation is consistent with confounding but does not identify it as the sole cause.

ICB-04.estimand: Conditional disorder-score contrast and dominant-residue exclusion decision across legacy whole-run seeds 0, 1, and 2.
ICB-04.statistical_unit: Source protein, nested within legacy whole-run seed.
ICB-04.control: Matched-norm random direction and residue-exclusion sensitivity analysis.
ICB-04.limitation: The same legacy seed changes the cohort split, masks, control direction, and bootstrap, so the result cannot be attributed to direction construction alone.

ICB-05.estimand: Primary and E/L-excluded conditional expression-score contrasts, with technical-failure and low-complexity risks over all attempts.
ICB-05.control: Matched-norm random direction and E/L residue-exclusion analysis.
ICB-05.limitation: An interval that includes zero is inconclusive. It does not prove that the remaining effect is zero. One direction build also cannot establish general seed sensitivity.

ICB-06.estimand: Overall and layer 30 through 32 cosine overlap for one fixed L55 and L57 direction pair.
ICB-06.statistical_unit: One fixed direction pair summarized over 33 paired layer vectors; layers are not independent replicates.
ICB-06.control: None. This is a descriptive pairwise diagnostic with no control-vector distribution.
ICB-06.limitation: One seed cannot support a robustness or causal claim.

INT-01.estimand: Layer-adjusted finite-head association between discovery-panel contact enrichment and independent-panel contact-specific zero-replacement damage across the 480 fixed heads.
INT-01.statistical_unit: Protein for outcome estimation; the 480 heads form one fixed finite set for the association.
INT-01.control: Matched non-contact positions within protein and discovery-matched control heads.
INT-01.limitation: The claim is limited to the frozen discovery and independent confirmation panels, matching rule, interventions, and model revision.

INT-02.estimand: Head-by-head contact-specific ablation equivalence between each prespecified top-five head and its matched controls under zero and mean replacement.
INT-02.control: At least two same-layer controls matched on discovery-only measurements.
INT-02.limitation: Equivalence requires every familywise-adjusted interval to lie inside the frozen margin and is not established by a non-significant difference.

INT-03.estimand: Independent-panel group-level contact-enrichment replication statistic for the frozen top-five head set.
INT-03.control: Frozen top-five set selected only from the discovery panel.
INT-03.limitation: The group result does not establish that every selected head replicates, and correlational replication does not establish causal importance.
